- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is below historical mean, increase forecast by 10–20% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is above historical mean, reduce forecast by 15–30% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp spike in sentiment or price, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 15–25% in next 3–5 days to allow for mean reversion.  
- If forecast shows persistent overestimation (e.g., > 20% above true value for 3+ consecutive days), apply downward bias correction proportional to sentiment decay.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, forecast should be anchored to 3–5 day moving average of recent history, not extrapolated.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model should adjust for volatility clustering — reduce forecast magnitude by 10–15% for next 5 days.
